finalText:
I've read the script-element pages on MDN and in the HTML Standard, plus the MDN pages for DOMContentLoaded and JavaScript modules. I'm writing up the answer now. The javascript.info URL from the plan returned a 404, so I haven't used it.

## Answer

**Default (neither attribute).** A classic `<script src>` with neither attribute blocks the parser. The spec says "If neither attribute is present, then the script is fetched and evaluated immediately, blocking parsing until these are both complete." (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). `async` and `defer` are both boolean attributes, so the presence of the attribute is what counts (same page).

**`async`.**
- *Parsing:* the script downloads in parallel with parsing. Per the spec, "if the async attribute is present, then the classic script will be fetched in parallel to parsing and evaluated as soon as it is available (potentially before parsing completes)." (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). Parsing is therefore interrupted only while the script runs, not while it downloads. That follows from the quoted sentence.
- *DOMContentLoaded:* there is no fixed relationship. MDN says DOMContentLoaded "doesn't wait for other things like images, subframes, and async scripts to finish loading." (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event).
- *Order:* the spec keeps async scripts in a *set* of scripts that will execute as soon as possible, and each one runs when its own result is ready. In the processing algorithm the async branch runs the script when its result is ready and does not check other scripts. So there is no ordering guarantee. This is my reading of the algorithm, not a sentence the spec states.

**`defer`.**
- *Parsing:* the script downloads in parallel and waits. The spec says "If the async attribute is not present but the defer attribute is present, then the classic script will be fetched in parallel and evaluated when the page has finished parsing." (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).
- *DOMContentLoaded:* MDN says defer means the script runs "after the document has been parsed, but before firing DOMContentLoaded event". It adds that deferred scripts "will prevent the DOMContentLoaded event from firing until the script has loaded and finished evaluating." (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script). The DOMContentLoaded page agrees: the event "is queued after deferred scripts" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event).
- *Order:* "Scripts with the defer attribute will execute in the order in which they appear in the document." (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script). The spec backs this up by appending each one to a *list* of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).

**Both attributes together.** MDN says "If the attribute is specified with the defer attribute, the element will act as if only the async attribute is specified." (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script). The spec says the combination is allowed so that legacy browsers that only support `defer` fall back to deferred behaviour instead of blocking (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).

**Inline classic scripts (no `src`).** `async` and `defer` do nothing. MDN's warning is that the attribute "must not be used if the src attribute is absent (i.e., for inline scripts), in this case it would have no effect." (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script). In the spec, an inline classic script is run at once: "Otherwise, immediately execute the script element el, even if other scripts are already executing." (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). That branch also covers an external script that has neither attribute and is ready.

**`type="module"` scripts.**
- *Deferred by default:* the spec says that without `async`, "the module script and its dependencies will be fetched in parallel to parsing and evaluated when the page has finished parsing." It also says "(The defer attribute has no effect on module scripts.)" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). MDN's modules guide agrees: "modules are deferred automatically." (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Modules).
- *Order and DOMContentLoaded:* modules without `async` go into the same list as deferred scripts. They run in document order, before DOMContentLoaded. MDN lists `<script type="module">` alongside `defer` scripts that DOMContentLoaded waits for.
- *`async` on modules:* `async` does apply. The module and all its dependencies are fetched in parallel and run as soon as they are ready, potentially before parsing completes (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). MDN says the same (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script).
- *Inline modules:* `async` and the module-specific behaviour still apply, because the spec's branch tests "el's type is "module"" and does not require `src`. An inline module is never run synchronously. The spec notes that "we won't proceed to execute the script element synchronously." So an inline module is deferred, or runs on arrival if it has `async` (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).

**Where the sources differ.** The spec says an async script may run "potentially before parsing completes", so it can run before DOMContentLoaded. MDN's DOMContentLoaded page is stricter in two places. One note says the event "is fired after the execution of these scripts, but before the execution of scripts with async." Elsewhere it says that for `<script async>` "by the time it executes, DOMContentLoaded has already fired." (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event). I'd treat the spec as authoritative. The practical rule is that an async script may run before or after DOMContentLoaded, so check `document.readyState` before relying on the event.

**Plan departure.** The plan's `javascript.info` source was unavailable, so the DOMContentLoaded claims rest on MDN and the spec.
